skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Guides authors, reviewers, and team leads through practical pull request review workflows.
skill.summary: Structured code review playbook for clearer pull requests and faster, higher quality reviews.

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, example shell snippets, relative documentation links, CODEOWNERS patterns, and environment template filenames. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden execution, or unsafe filesystem access was found in the reviewed context. The skill is process guidance for pull requests and code review, with visible project-check examples.

content.value_statement: Slow, unclear reviews delay releases and miss defects. This skill gives authors, reviewers, and team leads practical workflows for focused pull requests.
actual_capabilities: Guides authors through pre-PR tests, linting, type checks, scope review, and description quality.
Provides a two-pass reviewer process for design, security, correctness, testing, and readability.
Defines review comment labels such as critical, issue, suggestion, nit, question, and praise.
Includes PR, CODEOWNERS, author checklist, and reviewer checklist templates.
Suggests team adoption steps, review SLAs, and review health metrics.
limitations: It does not enforce CI, branch protection, or repository policy by itself.
Command examples depend on scripts and tools that already exist in the user repository.
CODEOWNERS guidance must be adapted to real team names and ownership boundaries.
It is process guidance and checklist support, not a standalone security scanner.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Run a structured author checklist before opening a pull request, including tests, scope, documentation, and risk notes.

use_cases.title: Review Complex Changes
use_cases.description: Use a two-pass review method to assess design first, then implementation details and test quality.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reviews
use_cases.description: Create shared templates, reviewer ownership, review SLAs, and practical metrics for a team review process.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Pull Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner author wants a readiness check before opening a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-review skill to check my branch before I open a pull request. Focus on scope, tests, description quality, and reviewer readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Guide My Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Reviewer needs a clear process for a normal pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-review skill to guide my review of this pull request. Start with design and risk, then move to implementation, tests, and readability.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Reviewer wants comments that are clear and easy to act on.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the comment classification guidance to rewrite my review feedback. Label each item as critical, issue, suggestion, nit, question, or praise.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Team Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Team lead wants a repeatable review process across a team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-review skill to design a team review workflow. Include PR templates, CODEOWNERS guidance, review SLAs, metrics, and adoption steps.

output_examples.input: Author asks for a pre-PR readiness review.
output: Readiness summary with pass, warning, and blocker items.
Checklist covering tests, scope, documentation, deployment notes, and security considerations.
Suggested reviewers based on ownership areas and change risk.

output_examples.input: Reviewer asks for help reviewing an authentication pull request.
output: Pass one findings about design, authorization risk, and scope.
Pass two findings about logic, error handling, test coverage, and naming.
Final recommendation with comments grouped by severity label.

output_examples.input: Team lead asks how to roll out better code reviews.
output: Adoption plan for a small pilot, team rollout, and ongoing measurement.
Recommended review SLAs and pull request size targets.
Template checklist for author and reviewer expectations.

best_practices: Use small, focused pull requests with clear context, test plans, and rollback notes.
Review design and risk before commenting on implementation details.
Classify comments so authors know what must change and what is optional.
anti_patterns: Opening large pull requests with weak context and no self-review.
Blocking on style nits that should be handled by automated tooling.
Tracking raw comment counts instead of useful review outcomes.

faq.question: Does this skill replace human code review?
faq.answer: No. It guides review preparation and review structure, but humans still decide risk, design fit, and merge readiness.

faq.question: Can it run my project tests?
faq.answer: It can suggest visible local quality gates. Actual command execution depends on the AI tool, repository scripts, and user approval.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What review method does it use?
faq.answer: It uses a two-pass method. Review design, scope, and risk first, then check implementation, tests, and readability.

faq.question: Can it help create templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for pull request templates, CODEOWNERS, author checklists, and reviewer checklists.

faq.question: Is it a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It includes security review prompts, but it does not replace SAST, secret scanning, dependency scanning, or manual security review.
